out.other_title: Multiagent debate between LLM instances improves reasoning and factual accuracy
out.rationale: Du et al. report multi-agent debate improves reasoning and factuality over single-agent baselines. Smit et al. report no protocol dominates on seven QA datasets, Medprompt performs best overall, and the debating protocols (Society of Minds, Multi-Persona, ChatEval) do not outperform others on the reasoning datasets; Smit et al. include self-consistency and ensembling baselines that Du et al. do not.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate reliably improves LLM reasoning and factuality over other prompting strategies

out.other_title: MAD raises counter-intuitive arithmetic accuracy from 26% to 37%, below GPT-4's 51%
out.rationale: Liang et al. report MAD raises CIAR accuracy from 26% to 37% with GPT-3.5-Turbo, above self-consistency (29.5%). Smit et al. include CIAR among their reasoning datasets and report the debating protocols (SoM, Multi-Persona, ChatEval) do not outperform other protocols there; Smit et al. pick the best configuration per system and compare with more baselines such as Medprompt and ensemble refinement.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate beats self-consistency on counter-intuitive arithmetic reasoning (CIAR) with GPT-3.5
